title: Male borrowers who mention providing electricity or cell phone charging services may fund faster.
Mentioning specific educational fees, such as college registration, may decelerate funding for women.
Female borrowers who mention specific towns or districts may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who write shorter pitches may fund faster than those who write longer ones.
Female borrowers who explicitly promise prompt repayment may fund faster.
Providing specific demographic details, such as age or family member employment, predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning marital status or the existence of children may decelerate funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their age or birth year in the pitch text may experience faster funding.
Female borrowers who include explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about children's ages or education may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayments predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Female borrowers who mention local currency amounts or specific institutional affiliations fund more slowly.
Male borrowers who provide detailed narrative explanations of business processes fund more slowly.
